PLAN · lines as rigged at Kitano-jima
BOW ELEVATION · as in the screenshot
looking aft from the pier · port on the right · lines as rigged
The laid ramp’s lowest point is 0.000 m clear of what it lies on (the flap’s toe, on the asphalt); the girders now taper above the pier.
PIER, in section: deck 0.59 m (world), 0.5 m thick; face 1.90 m ahead of the stem
cargo court asphalt, +0.07 over the pier
DETAIL A · the ramp’s toe on the pier
FINDINGS · Rev A found them, Rev B fixed them; measured again from the game model
At Kitano-jima the after spring and stern line ran through the ship

Rev A: the aft station’s two lines were led from the port-quarter fairlead to pier bitts ahead of the bow: 37.88 and 37 m through the aft mooring station, casing P, the lower lobby and across the car deck (10 and 9 modelled faces), the yellow line in the screenshot. The Minato head line also bent in the air over the port bow house’s roof edge, clipping it.

Rev B: each station keeps its own two ropes (ferry.js FERRY_MOORING.ropes); bow-on at Kitano-jima she makes fast from both bows only, each led through its stem fairlead to the bitts on its own side, the bosun at the starboard bow, the stern ropes coiled aft; Minato’s head line and forward spring lead through a new side chock on the bow house’s corner; the coils moved clear of
Now: 0 modelled faces pierced by any laid line at Kitano-jima or Minato, ramp raised or laid (tests/ferry-exterior.test.mjs).
The bridge name board’s two names ran into each other

Rev A: みなと丸 and MINATO MARU were each centred on fixed points of the 512 px board (30% and 72%); in Helvetica Bold (an iPad) the English started at 238.7 px and 丸 ended at 263.5 px, about 25 px of overlap.

Rev B: the names are laid out from their measured widths, centred as a pair with 30 px between them inside a 34 px margin, both shrinking together if a device’s font is wider (src/world/ferry-boards.js nameBoardLayout).
Now: 26.3 px between the names in Chromium’s fonts, 26.1 px in Helvetica Bold.
The lane boards’ truck sign sat across a lane divider

Rev A: the truck pictogram was drawn beside the middle arrow’s foot, its cab (x 326–348 px) across the divider (329–335 px), 0.18 m tall: from the quay it read as a stray “L” on the arrow. The dividers were 7 px off the middle between the lanes.
Rev B: a larger truck under a shortened centre arrow, centred in its lane; the dividers midway between the lanes (src/world/ferry-boards.js laneBoardLayout).
Now: the truck spans x 198–314 px, 22 and 22 px clear of the dividers.
The ramp’s side girders ran into the pier

Rev A: the leaf’s two side girders, 0.5 m deep for its whole 4 m and square at the toe, ended 0.28 m inside the Kitano-jima pier deck and 0.33 m below Minato’s landing plate; the flap’s hinge pin sank 0.02 m into the landing.

Rev B: the girders taper over the leaf’s last 2 m to the deck plate’s own depth at the toe, the plate’s underside eases up over its last 0.3 m, the flap’s hinge pin is flush with its underside, and the plate is 4.4 m clear between the girders.
Now: lowest point of the laid ramp 0.000 m over the Kitano-jima pier, 0.000 m over Minato’s landing plate.

The owner’s screenshot of 3 November 2026, surveyed again
Her pose is the game’s: on her waterline at rest, the ramp laid on the Kitano-jima pier by restRamp(), the lines laid bitt → fairlead →
pier bitt as createFerryRun lays them (FERRY_MOORINGS.airport). Green: found in Rev A and fixed, measured again. Red: still open. Red
dashed: a faulty line where it is hidden inside or behind her; × where a line pierces a modelled face (none now).
AS-BUILT SURVEY OF THE GAME MODEL · Johansson World vessel · no flag, class or construction approval · drawn by projecting buildFerryModel() with hidden lines removed
